chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:

Abū Ḥanīfah entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him: “What do you say about a house that collapsed upon a people, and two boys remained from them, one of them free and the other owned by his master, but it was not known which was the free one and which was the owned one?” Abū Ḥanīfah said: “Half of this one and half of that one should be freed, and the wealth should be divided equally between them in two halves.” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It is not like that. Rather, lots are to be cast between them, so whichever one the lot falls upon, he is the free one; and this one is freed and made a mawlā to him.”

key_terms.الْقُرْعَةُ: drawing lots to determine a legal outcome when identity is uncertain
key_terms.مَوْلًى لَهُ: affiliated client of the free person after emancipation
key_terms.يُقْسَمُ الْمَالُ: the estate or property is divided

ai.seo_question: How does Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rule when the free person and the slave cannot be distinguished after a fatal house collapse?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling on an inheritance and status dispute when two boys survive a house collapse and it is unknown which one is free and which one is enslaved. Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects speculative division and instead rules that القرعة should determine the free person, after which the other is emancipated and attached to him as a mawlā.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5660 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, who said:

Abu Hanifah entered upon Abu Abdullah (as), and Abu Abdullah (as) asked him:
"What do you say about a house that collapsed on a group of people, leaving behind two boys - one of them is free and the other is a slave belonging to the free one - but it is not known which is the free one and which is the slave?"
Abu Hanifah replied: "Half of this one and half of that one should be freed, and the wealth should be divided equally between them."
Abu Abdullah (as) said: "It is not so. Rather, a draw (lot) should be cast between them, and the one upon whom the lot falls is the free one, and the other is freed and made his client (mawla)."
